claims: 最新 version 21 状态 Under Discussion (Re-Opened)；2026-09-18 version19 已有强制 consolidation 重写稿，主窗口2026-09-30 version20 继续修订，10-02 version21 新增事务仍属后续工作。

sources.title: Disk-Based LSMs: An Unexpectedly Good Index for Partly Coherent CXL Memory
claims: SOSP 2026 paper, DOI 10.1145/3830418.3843886; official September 30 schedule provides event attribution.
SCR hardware-coherent region and LNR noncoherent region expose a tradeoff between fine-grained version metadata capacity and coarse-grained false invalidation.
Prism bounds the updatable surface: a hot-key memtable in SCR, bounded updatable layer in LNR with versions in SCR, and immutable SSTables in LNR with manifest and monotonically increasing IDs.
New keys enter BUL and repeatedly written keys are promoted to the memtable; tier transitions make new location readable before removing old location.
Default evaluation emulates three hosts and shared memory on four-socket Xeon Gold 6418H, 128MB SCR, 100M 24-byte keys / 100-byte values, Zipf 0.99.
At 50% writes, peak microbenchmark throughput is up to 6.2x SC-BTree; SC-BTree wins short range scans at 5% writes.
Any host or memory device failure halts the full system; all data is volatile, recovery/durability outside scope.
Actual underlying hardware is coherent; incorrect cache-maintenance protocols require separate model checking to expose stale reads.
sources.access_notes: Downloaded full 18-page author-hosted publication-format PDF; read introduction and §§2–5.7, implementation, §§7.1–7.8 and failure model. First page includes ACM DOI, ISBN and SOSP 2026 reference; final official schedule links same DOI. The event_date is scheduled presentation September 30, not a claimed first PDF date. Experiments are author-reported, not independently reproduced. Python model checking of the protocol is finite testing evidence, not a new end-to-end durability proof.

sources.title: Borges: A Low-Latency Distributed Shared Log on a CXL Memory/SSD Hybrid
claims: SOSP 2026 paper, DOI 10.1145/3830418.3843906; scheduled September 30.
Single-writer shared metadata avoids cross-host multi-writer atomics in noncoherent CXL; each append is replicated before being sequenced.

Sequencer consumes per-shard minimum replicated progress, constructs private back index, persists replicated global cut, then publishes corresponding reader-visible index/cut; acknowledgments follow publication.
RCU-style readers announce the chosen index then recheck it; writers wait for old readers before index reuse; leases handle failed readers.
Evaluation: Xeon 6761P with eight VMs, each 5 vCPU and 10GB DRAM, physical 1TB Samsung CMM-H on PCIe5 x8, 10GbE client/server TCP/IP.

Append setup uses 2 shards, 2 replicas, 100B payload. Table4 low-load P99 184.21us vs Scalog-CXL 528.57us; saturated throughput 161.91K vs 74.96K requests/s, using different client counts from low-load latency.
Scaling beyond six physical-testbed shard servers uses synthetic shard streams for 8,12,16; 16-shard data is not a real 16-host deployment.
Recovery tests kill a shard server and add a shard; no separate sequencer restart benchmark reported.
sources.access_notes: Downloaded full 18-page author-hosted published-format PDF; read §§1–3.8 (especially publication, replay, failure model), §4.1–4.3 and Tables3–4, §§4.8–4.10 and Table7. First page carries ACM DOI/ISBN and publication pages. Final official schedule links same DOI. Local eight-VM pod emulation with a real storage device does not independently establish real multi-host/multi-device failure-domain behavior. CMM-H persistence is a hardware model/premise of the paper; no independent power-loss test was performed here. event_date reflects presentation slot, not first release.

sources.title: DiaLSM: Towards Write-Stall-Free Performance via Shard-based LSM-tree — full paper
claims: Internal hash-sharded independent LSM pipelines with dynamic fallback to non-stalled shards, indexed by Clue Entries in the primary shard.
2MB reserved memtable space for ~100000 20-byte CEs; L0 capping and CE cache reduce indirection cost.
Rollback returns fallback values to primary; conflicts with newer foreground versions must be handled; CE threshold can stop new CEs and reintroduce stalls.
Implementation on RocksDB8.3.2; platform dual AMD EPYC7352,256GB DDR4,3.84TB Samsung Gen3x4 NVMe SSD,CentOS7/ext4.
Author reports FillRandom maximum2.4x throughput and94.3% stall reduction against ADOC.
Evaluation disables throttling thresholds,commit logging,and block cache; results cannot directly establish durable-production benefit.
Paper discusses shared-device bandwidth saturation, read/write/space amplification, recovery and shard-count deployment tradeoffs.
sources.access_notes: Downloaded full15-page PDF and extracted text. Read §II modeling assumptions, §III-A–F design/CE handling/rollback/range scans/failure recovery, §IV-A experimental setup including disabled logging and cache, performance discussion and §VI. No independent code execution or crash testing. Distinguish author-reported recovery design from empirically demonstrated power-loss durability. Do not interpret vacation-queue model as unconditional proof that every load necessarily stalls. No official ICDE2027 proceedings checked.
